analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump (line 3) and a new paragraph at head lines 874-878 in the GLM section. The paragraph says GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls renders OpenRouter-returned reasoning (`reasoning` / `reasoning_details` text) on earlier assistant turns as the template's `reasoning_content`. It also says `strict` tools are served by validating each `auto` call against its schema before exposure (ToolConstraintValidation.validate), not by constraining decoding. No executable code is in the supplied evidence, so no control was observed to be weakened. The statement that strict tools are validated and not constrained is honest and does not overclaim; it matches the existing paragraph at base lines 865-871 that the parser does not implement constrained decoding. Threat-model relevance is limited: A-001 (prompts) and TB-002/TB-007. Prior-turn reasoning becomes template input on the provider after coordinator decryption, which is within the existing trust model, where the provider sees plaintext prompts. It does not touch the prefix-cache scope or the T-041 SSD cache. Remaining integration questions I could not verify, since the code changes are outside this batch: (1) whether returnedReasoning is length-bounded and sanitized, so injected reasoning cannot break template framing or inflate prompt size past admission limits; (2) whether the strict-tool validation fails closed on a schema-validation error; (3) whether the code changes in this PR keep the tokenizer preflight (`GLM5NextTokenizerPreflight`) and the shipped-template hash check (`requireShippedTemplate`) intact. No finding is warranted from the documentation change alone.
